question: Should ClickClack support separate persistent alignment controls for the current user and all other human and agent participants?
rationale: Adding a second permanent appearance preference and grouping teammates with agents establishes a product and UX contract that cannot be inferred from existing behavior alone.

options.title: Sponsor independent controls
options.body: Accept the two-control model, then require visible browser proof, geometry-level coverage, and removal of the changelog edit before merge.

options.title: Keep one alignment control
options.body: Retain the existing self-message preference and close or redesign this PR to avoid expanding the settings surface.

options.title: Choose different participant groups
options.body: Define a maintainer-approved alignment model for self, humans, and agents before implementation continues.

recommendation.title: Sponsor independent controls
recommendation.body: Accept the two-control model, then require visible browser proof, geometry-level coverage, and removal of the changelog edit before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a chat UX and persistent-settings decision, and steipete is the best available routing candidate from repository-level history.
